purpose: Define a non-secret, non-authorizing collection sequence for every target-environment evidence category tracked by the production-readiness manifest.
global_prohibited_actions_without_separa: Create or modify a production Tasks identity, Viewer membership, bearer credential, or Vaultwarden item.
Create, replace, expose, copy, or reveal a reusable production secret or recovery credential.
Create or modify production Docker networks, DNS, Caddy, NetBird, firewall, monitoring, notification, backup, or scheduling state.
Deploy, activate, restart, stop, remove, or migrate the production Tasks service or production data.
Perform a destructive restore, rollback, failover, outage injection, or recovery exercise against a production environment.
Mark a target-evidence item satisfied or mark production approved without separately authorized evidence and review.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud VPS — System and Environment Record
GoreeCloud — Inventory — Listening Ports and Active Network Services
success_criteria: The actual target host identity, operating system, runtime versions, active listeners, and relevant service state are observed directly.
The evidence distinguishes live observations from historical inventory values and does not expose reusable secrets.
Final owner UID, service-readable group/GID, protected paths, modes, ACLs where applicable, and read-only secret mounts are observed directly.
Only metadata and approved path references are recorded; active secret values are excluded.
Docker Engine and Compose versions, image references, container user/capabilities, restart policy, mounts, networks, health state, and published-port state are observed from the target runtime.
The observation confirms no unexpected backend or database host-port exposure.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud Private Web Service Publication Standard
success_criteria: The approved tasks.goreecloud.com private DNS result is observed from an approved client path and matched to the intended target endpoint.
The authoritative DNS record is synchronized after validation without inventing an unobserved address.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud — Inventory — NetBird Peers, Groups, and Access Policies
success_criteria: The target peer, approved client/group membership, applicable access policy, and observed source path are recorded from current NetBird state.
The evidence demonstrates least-privilege reachability without treating NetBird membership as application authorization.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud — Reference — DNS and HTTPS Responsibilities
success_criteria: The production certificate chain, hostname/SAN, issuer, validity, and DNS-01 ownership path are verified without exposing the Porkbun credential value.
The evidence confirms a publicly trusted certificate for the exact Tasks hostname.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud — Inventory — Listening Ports and Active Network Services
success_criteria: The active Caddy configuration path, site/listener ownership, host port bindings, and nftables behavior are observed on the target host.
The evidence confirms Caddy remains the controlled HTTP/HTTPS gateway and no competing direct Tasks publication path exists.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud Private Web Service Publication Standard
success_criteria: An approved NetBird client reaches https://tasks.goreecloud.com over trusted TLS through the intended private publication path.
A non-approved source is denied, backend/database ports remain non-public, and the application authentication and CSRF boundaries behave as designed.

Approved acceptance identities verify private personal workspaces, explicit shared-project membership, role enforcement, assignment boundaries, and revocation behavior through the real publication path.
Acceptance uses controlled non-sensitive test content and does not grant broader access than required.
The real Tasks monitor uses the approved private health URL, observed monitoring source, final retry/timeout values, and intended notification assignment.
An approved administrator receives sanitized DOWN and RECOVERED notifications, and monitor rollback/removal is proven.
The approved production recovery-point mechanism, repository/location, schedule, retention, encryption posture, monitoring, and notification receipt are verified.
A successful recovery point is shown usable rather than merely present.
At least one required recovery copy is independent of the primary Tasks host and failure domain.
The evidence records independence and recoverability without copying repository credentials into ordinary records.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud Vaultwarden Sensitive Information Storage Standard
success_criteria: The credentials required to recover Tasks and its protected backup path are independently available through approved protected storage.
Only credential record references and recovery-test results are documented; active values are not copied into evidence.
When the Infrastructure Services VM exists on Proxmox, an applicable VM-level backup is verified and a recovery path involving the approved backup system is demonstrated.
The evidence distinguishes VM-level recovery from application/database recovery.
A separately approved material recovery exercise reconstructs the production environment from trusted recovery points and independently available configuration/credentials.
The resulting record passes the Production Recovery Evidence Contract before it can support a GO decision.
After recovery, backup protection resumes and produces a new verified recovery point distinct from the recovery source.
Monitoring returns to the expected protected state before recovery is considered complete.

evidence_sources: GoreeCloud VPS — System and Environment Record
success_criteria: Current storage/capacity headroom is recorded and a material recovery exercise records elapsed recovery time against any approved objective.
No unapproved RTO or RPO value is invented when the authoritative records do not establish one.
The dedicated non-interactive Tasks identity, approved Viewer memberships, protected bearer credential, manager-tasks network path, and read-only authorization behavior are validated together.
Manager remains unable to select another Tasks identity, bypass project membership, or gain database access.
The production Tasks notification publisher identity, least-privilege ACL, schedule/reminder behavior, and approved end-client receipt are validated.
Notification content remains minimized and reusable credentials are excluded from payloads and evidence.
Authoritative inventories, configuration records, recovery records, project status, and change logs agree with the observed production state.
Every satisfied manifest item has a non-secret authoritative evidence reference, verifier, and timezone-aware verification timestamp.
